name: Side By Side
label: Revelation
lede: Side By Side lasted about a year and a half and split before their only record came out. That seven-song 7" has been repressed for nearly four decades.

eras.title: Five months from first show to first band
eras.text: Jules Massee, a kid from Weehawken, New Jersey, saw his first hardcore show on Long Island in early summer 1986. About five months later he was fronting a band out of an Alphabet City apartment, in the youngest wave of New York straight edge.

years.h: Jules Massee sees his first hardcore show at the Right Track Inn
years.p: The bill on Long Island is [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]], [[Straight Ahead|1fd60d7c-dc35-44f5-9162-4113b6ca4a69]] and [[Sick of It All|e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7]].

years.h: An Alphabet City apartment becomes Side By Side
years.p: Massee sings, Eric Fink plays guitar and Billy Bitter plays bass. Drummer Gavin is borrowed from NY Hoods for the early stretch.

years.src: In Effect Hardcore · Wikipedia: Sammy Siegler
years.p: Siegler, born in 1973, is barely into his teens. He'll go on to play in Youth of Today, [[Judge|3827fbb6-e219-4e2d-9af8-35cc9a7d8d8e]], [[Gorilla Biscuits|0320a32e-b781-40df-bf48-5cb5ee842762]] and CIV.
years.xp:
The sources don't date the swap from Gavin to Siegler, so 1986 is the best fit.

Within months of the band ending, Siegler was in Youth of Today.

eras.title: On the first Rev roll call
eras.text: Revelation Records' second release put the new straight edge New York bands on one 7", Side By Side among them. They shared bills with Youth of Today, Gorilla Biscuits and Warzone all year, then went into Don Fury's studio.

years.src: Revelation Records: pressing history · In Effect Hardcore
years.h: Side By Side's first record is a comp: New York City Hardcore: Together
years.p: Revelation's second release. The first press was 600 black and 400 orange, the orange being the 'gold' vinyl collectors still confuse with the later yellow.
years.xp: In Effect says the comp also carried a track called 'Violence To Fade' for Side By Side, but that title isn't confirmed elsewhere.

years.h: Kids push the bouncers off the CBGB stage
years.p: After a lawsuit, CBGB's owner hires bouncers to stop stage diving. At the first note of Gorilla Biscuits' set, Massee says, the kids bum-rush them off, and the matinees are briefly halted.
years.xp: Massee puts the night on a bill with Youth of Today, Gorilla Biscuits and Pagan Babies. The source doesn't date it or name the lawsuit, so 1987 is a best fit.

years.p: Brown rounds out the line-up and soon joins Gorilla Biscuits too. He isn't on the EP, which Massee says was cut by the original four.

eras.title: Gone before the record came out
eras.text: The band drifted apart after the session, with no fight and no final night planned as one. The EP landed after it was over, and the members were already feeding the next wave of bands.

q: It wasn't poetic, it wasn't complicated... but it was genuine.
yt: Live at the Anthrax, Norwalk CT, Aug 28, 1987
years.h: "It wasn't poetic," Massee says of the end, but the last show was the best
years.p: The final official show is at the Anthrax, a Connecticut club, and the band remembers it as the best they ever played.
years.xp:
There was no dramatic ending. The members drifted apart, and You're Only Young Once... was already recorded.

Siegler landed in Youth of Today within months, and Brown was already playing in Gorilla Biscuits. The clip here is the band at the Anthrax a few months before that last night.

years.h: You're Only Young Once... arrives after the split
years.p: [[Don Fury|0bec484f-b890-4823-af64-0e48530f6f6f]] recorded the seven songs in 1987. Revelation put them out as REV 5 in 1988, with the band already over.
years.xp:
Two songs the band played, Guilty and Good Clean Fun, never got recorded, nor did a Youth Brigade cover. The first press came in two batches of 1,005 and 1,012, about a week apart, some with one of at least three stickers.

Two more 2,000-copy presses followed: silver labels and a cover opening at the bottom on the second, grey labels and a black border around the back-cover live photo on the third.

years.h: Side By Side, Gorilla Biscuits and Bold live at the Anthrax, Norwalk CT, January 15, 1988
yt: Side By Side, Gorilla Biscuits and Bold live at the Anthrax, Norwalk CT, January 15, 1988

years.h: Massee plays a benefit for [[Roger Miret|ab51d57f-5007-4ee4-8461-a4050f8d939d]] at CBGB
years.p: Massee is back on the CBGB stage for a show benefiting [[Agnostic Front|40b8a690-94e4-4c82-ad0f-73f4b841e46a]] singer Roger Miret. He dates it to 1989 but doesn't say what the benefit was for.
About a year after Side By Side split, he forms the new band with [[Lars Weiss|c60d8790-7786-4df8-8647-7f8b2ca02c17]], who'd go on to Uppercut and Judge.

eras.title: The 7" that kept coming back
eras.text: With the band long gone, You're Only Young Once... became a Revelation evergreen, back in print on new colors of vinyl. Brown became a painter whose work reached MoMA.

years.p: Revelation's first 12" edition: 1,109 on black vinyl and 100 on blue.
550 copies on red, then grey in 2013 and gold in 2017.
Civ said Brown died suddenly of a basal ganglia stroke, correcting early reports of an aneurysm. He was by then a painter shown in New York, Tokyo, Geneva and Brussels.
years.xp:
He is remembered through the Alex Brown Foundation, an artist residency in Des Moines, Iowa, where he was born.

Sources differ on the date: Mainframe Studios says January 30, 2019, while Gorilla Biscuits' Wikipedia page says September 4.

eras.title: Three shows, then done
eras.text: Massee, by now a lawyer in Florida, had no plans to play again. A benefit for the late Alex Brown brought the originals back for three shows across two continents, and they called the last one the last.

years.big: "I never had any intention of playing with Side By Side again."
q: I never had any intention of playing with Side By Side again.
years.h: The originals reunite for Alex Brown
years.p: Massee, Fink, Billy Bitter and Siegler, with Weiss on second guitar, play Revolution Calling in the Netherlands in late November for the Alex Brown Foundation.
years.xp: Weiss had played bass at the band's last show in the '80s and took Brown's guitar spot this time. Massee's conditions, he told No Echo, were the original line-up and a charitable purpose in Brown's memory.

years.h: Thirty-five years on, a benefit at the Monarch in Brooklyn
years.p: Side By Side headline the show, 35 years after You're Only Young Once... came out.

years.h: Last show at 1720 in Los Angeles, on a bill with Youth of Today
years.p: Night two of Revelation's weekend at 1720 is billed as Side By Side's final reunion show.
years.xp: The weekend was The Book of Revelation Records. Side By Side shared the night with Youth of Today.
